what: Why? Selection Bias in Phase Transitions
title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
text: Consider simple example. Units transition “inactive” “active” probability depending covariate xx: P(transition|x)=logit−1(β0+β1x)P(\text{transition} | x) = \text{logit}^{-1}(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x) outcomes depend phase xx: Inactive: y∼N(μ0+γ0x,σ02)y \sim N(\mu_0 + \gamma_0 x, \sigma_0^2) Active: y∼N(μ1+γ1x,σ12)y \sim N(\mu_1 + \gamma_1 x, \sigma_1^2) problem: units observe phase random. Units certain xx values likely transition. naively compare “” vs “” outcomes, confound phase effect selection effect.

title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
code: library(phaseR) set.seed(42)  # Simulate data where transition probability depends on x # and outcomes depend on both phase AND x n_units <- 200 n_times <- 6  # True parameters beta_trans <- c(-1.5, 1.2)  # x increases transition probability beta_inactive <- c(10, 2)   # y = 10 + 2*x in inactive phase beta_active <- c(8, 2)      # y = 8 + 2*x in active phase (same slope!) # True "effect" of activation = -2 (intercept shift only)  dat <- sim_phaseR(   n_units = n_units,   n_times = n_times,   beta_trans = beta_trans,   beta_0 = beta_inactive,   beta_1 = beta_active,   sigma_0 = 1.5,   sigma_1 = 1.5,   seed = 123 )  # How many units transitioned? n_transitioned <- length(unique(dat$id[dat$true_phase == 1])) cat("Units that transitioned:", n_transitioned, "of", n_units, "\n") #> Units that transitioned: 149 of 200

title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
text: researcher might analyze units transitioned, comparing outcomes vs : naive estimate biased! units transitioned systematically different xx values didn’t, xx affects transition probability outcomes.
code:
# Get units that transitioned transitioned_ids <- unique(dat$id[dat$true_phase == 1])  # For each transitioned unit, compare before vs after naive_effects <- sapply(transitioned_ids, function(uid) {   unit_dat <- dat[dat$id == uid, ]    # Find transition point   trans_time <- min(which(unit_dat$true_phase == 1))    # Average outcome before (if any observations in phase 0)   before_obs <- unit_dat$true_phase == 0   after_obs <- unit_dat$true_phase == 1    if (sum(before_obs) > 0 && sum(after_obs) > 0) {     mean(unit_dat$y[after_obs]) - mean(unit_dat$y[before_obs])   } else {     NA   } })  naive_ate <- mean(naive_effects, na.rm = TRUE) cat("Naive before-after estimate:", round(naive_ate, 2), "
") #> Naive before-after estimate: -1.01 cat("True effect:", -2, "
") #> True effect: -2 cat("Bias:", round(naive_ate - (-2), 2), "
") #> Bias: 0.99

title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
text: selection mechanism creates confounding: Units higher xx likely transition (β1>0\beta_1 > 0). Since xx also affects outcomes (slope = 2 phases), “” observations transitioned units systematically higher yy ’d expect chance.
code: # Compare x values for transitioned vs non-transitioned units transitioned <- dat$id %in% transitioned_ids dat_first <- dat[dat$time == 1, ] dat_first$transitioned <- dat_first$id %in% transitioned_ids  cat("Mean x for transitioned units:",     round(mean(dat_first$x[dat_first$transitioned]), 2), "\n") #> Mean x for transitioned units: -0.01 cat("Mean x for non-transitioned units:",     round(mean(dat_first$x[!dat_first$transitioned]), 2), "\n") #> Mean x for non-transitioned units: -0.09

title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
text: phaseR models generative process - transition mechanism outcome dynamics - integrates phase uncertainty:
code:
model <- phase_model(   phases("inactive", "active"),   transition("inactive", "active", ~ x),   dynamics("inactive", y ~ x),   dynamics("active", y ~ x) )  # Fit the model (using short chain for vignette) fit <- fit_phaseR(model, data = dat, chains = 1, iter = 500, warmup = 250, seed = 456)  # Extract the effect (difference in intercepts) beta_inactive_est <- mean(fit$draws[, "beta_inactive_(Intercept)"]) beta_active_est <- mean(fit$draws[, "beta_active_(Intercept)"]) phaser_effect <- beta_active_est - beta_inactive_est  cat("phaseR estimate of effect:", round(phaser_effect, 2), "
") #> phaseR estimate of effect: -1.93 cat("True effect:", -2, "
") #> True effect: -2 cat("Bias:", round(phaser_effect - (-2), 2), "
") #> Bias: 0.07

title: Why Conditioning on Realized Change Fails
text: -comparisons condition realized transitions, introduces selection bias transition probability depends covariates. “effect” naive analysis valid causal estimand - conflates true phase effect selection effects. phaseR models complete generative process, properly accounting selection mechanism producing valid inference. applies broadly: disease onset studies, technology adoption, behavioral change, ecological regime shifts, etc. analysis stratifies realized outcomes risks bias.

title: Phase-Structured Inference for Longitudinal Change
text: longitudinal change switch regimes phaseR fits Bayesian models change longitudinal data, disease onset recovery, treatment adoption ecological regime shift, unit moves “” regime “” regime. package treats “” “” latent regimes models two things jointly: transition moves unit regimes, outcome dynamics within regime. likelihood sums regime observation may belong , estimates condition realized transition. Splitting data observed change point comparing two halves condition , biases comparison whenever chance transitioning depends covariates drive outcome. fit can estimate regime effects counterfactual outcomes, decide comparison answers question. phaseR supports: two regimes. Ordered phases phases("susceptible", "infected", "recovered"), one transition() per consecutive pair. Non-Gaussian outcomes. Gaussian, Poisson binomial dynamics, set per phase. Random effects. Random intercepts (1 | group), crossed (1 | site) + (1 | year), random slopes (1 + x | group) nested (1 | site/plot). Custom priors. prior() normal(), student_t(), cauchy(), half_normal(), half_cauchy() lkj(). Counterfactual effects. ate(), ite() counterfactual() predict outcomes covariate values never observed, integrating phase uncertainty. Model comparison. WAIC waic() compare_waic(), leave-one-cross-validation Pareto-smoothed importance sampling loo() loo_compare(). default backend -U-Turn sampler (NUTS), adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method, written C++ Rcpp, Stan, JAGS inference engine installed. Conditioning Realized Change Fails runs /estimate phaseR estimate known truth simulated data.
